parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Study Fig. 1.2, which shows information about population growth in The Gambia (an LEDC in
Africa).
The Gambia has had a consistently high population growth rate of 4.2% for
the last thirty years. 'The main reasons include polygamy, the fact that
the use of contraceptives is not common and a general reduction in infant
mortality rates.'
Since 1993 a family planning programme has attempted to increase the use
of modern contraceptives and reproductive health services in The Gambia. An
increase in the use of contraceptives has been achieved through community
health nurses and information campaigns.
Fig. 1.2

parts.label: (ii)
parts.text:

The Gambia, even though the use of contraception has recently increased.
